children: State-owned Kuwait Petroleum Corporation (KPC) and its subsidiaries increased their capital expenditure for the 2025/2026 fiscal year by nearly 21 percent.

KPC said in its annual report that capital spending swelled to nearly 2.3 billion Kuwaiti dinars ($7.5 billion) from around KWD 1.9 billion ($6.19 billion) in the 2024/2025 fiscal year, an increase of KWD 400 million year-on-year.

The increase occurred during a fiscal year in which KPC, and its subsidiaries recorded total revenues of KWD 32.7 billion and expenditures of KWD 30.5 billion, with net profit reaching KWD 2.2 billion.

“These figures reflect the scale of the financial and investment activity in the oil sector, as the capital expenditure recorded during the year represents about 7 percent of the total revenues of KPC and its subsidiaries, and is close to the net profit achieved during the same period,” Kuwait’s Al-Anba daily said.

Local content reached approximately 38 percent of total spending on goods, services and projects by the fourth quarter of 2025/26 fiscal while Kuwaiti drilling and maintenance companies accounted for 48 percent of the drilling rig fleet.

OPEC member Kuwait, which controls the world’s seventh largest proven oil deposits, has been locked in a drive to develop its hydrocarbon sector. The projects include boosting oil and gas capacity and building new petrochemical plants.
(Writing by N Saeed; Editing by Anoop Menon)
